content: For individuals without atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), heart failure (HF), or chronic kidney disease (CKD), the selection of medications should prioritize their effectiveness in achieving personalized blood glucose and weight management goals. Additionally, the choice of therapy should take into account the side effect profiles of the medications, particularly with respect to the risks of hypoglycemia and weight changes, as well as the cost of the treatment and the patient’s preferences. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/GLP-1 receptor agonists (GIP/GLP-1 RAs) have demonstrated significant efficacy in reducing hemoglobin A1C levels and promoting weight loss. Furthermore, newer formulations of these medications have shown durable effects and high levels of efficacy in clinical outcomes.
